title: Continuous Signal Matrix: Mapping Model Capabilities to Enterprise Use Cases
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Build a repeatable, living "signal matrix" that cross-references open and commercial model capabilities (latency, cost, instruction-following, tool-calling, hallucination rates, supported modalities) with high-priority enterprise use cases (search summarization, customer support, document Q&A, code generation, embeddings for semantic search). The output is a tracked artifact and process the PM and research team use to prioritize model onboarding, product compatibility recommendations, and GTM messaging.

This ticket covers scope 1 (MVP matrix and data pipelines), scope 2 (initial cadence and dashboards), and scope 3 (handoff to platform/console teams for productization).
deliverables: MVP Signal Matrix spreadsheet (fields + scoring rubric)
Automated ingestion pipeline spec (sheets -> BigQuery / Notion sync)
One-pager PRD describing use, owners, and decisions driven by the matrix
Dashboard prototype (Looker/Grafana) showing top signals by vertical
Quarterly review playbook and cadence document
acceptance_criteria: Matrix includes at least 12 distinct model variants (open/commercial) with standardized capability scores
Signal ingestion pipeline defined and owners assigned
Dashboard can be filtered by vertical and use case and shows delta week-over-week
Stakeholders (Sales, Solutions, Research, Platform) have reviewed and approved scoring rubric
Product team can map top 3 models to 5 prioritized enterprise use cases for Q2 roadmap decisions
research_plan: Inventory candidate models (Redwood catalog + top 6 external vendors) and capture public benchmarks
Design and run 5 focused evals per use case (prompt templates, failure modes, latency under constrained tokens)
Collect customer signals: closed-won RFIs, solutioning notes, support tickets mentioning model constraints
Interview 6 enterprise customers about friction points and must-have model attributes
Triangulate with cost-per-token and infra impact to create a cost-adjusted capability score
signals_to_track: Generation latency P50/P95 under typical request distributions
Token cost per effective output (cost / useful tokens)
Hallucination / factuality error rate for Q&A prompts
Compatibility with tool-calling and structured outputs
Embedding cosine separation for semantic search benchmarks
Observed customer adoption or asks for specific models
data_sources: Public model release notes and evaluation leaderboards
GitHub issues and PRs related to model regressions
notes: Trade-offs discussed: depth of per-model eval vs refresh cadence. Decided MVP will prioritize breadth (12 models) with lighter-weight evals, then iterate.
Scoring rubric will use weighted signals: reliability(30%), latency/cost(25%), accuracy(30%), integrations/tooling(15%). Weights are tentative and subject to stakeholder review.
We need to anonymize any customer examples shown on public dashboards; internal dashboards can include customer IDs behind SSO.
Potential product implication: surface 'recommended model by use-case' in Console and API defaults. Requires platform work later.
